Yes, the Artemis II crew successfully splashed down (landed) in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. ET, completing a historic 10-day mission around the Moon. The four-astronaut crew did not land on the Moon, but they safely returned to Earth. Key Details of the Mission: Mission Goal: A crewed flyby around the Moon to test systems, not a lunar landing. Splashdown Location: Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California. Crew: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch (NASA), and Jeremy Hansen (Canadian Space Agency). Significance: First humans to travel to the Moon and return to Earth since 1972. Future Missions: The upcoming Artemis III mission is expected to be the crewed lunar landing. Note: This refers to the Artemis II mission completed in April 2026. Artemis I was an uncrewed flight around the Moon in 2022.
